document.title: Show copy, move, and rename in the diff
document.summary: The live diff records git's rename, copy, and moved-line marks, and the UI shows that relationship on the file.
document.why: A unified diff shows a move as a full delete plus a full add. [#110](source:s1) asks the review to show the relationship git already knows.

sources.title: [Compre] Show copy/move/rename cleanly in the diff UI
sources.gist: Show a copy, move, or rename as relocated content, using git's own detection, without storing patch text.

lookFor: Subtle. [#110](source:s1) asks the UI to mark relocated content, and the line text stays the live git diff.

groups.title: The diff shows the relationship
groups.why: The reader sees those git marks on the file, so a move reads as one relationship.
groups.summary: Headers show Renamed, Moved, or Copied with the similarity. A moved block shows one chip. A pure path change has no line body.

commits.subject: Show git renames, copies, and moved lines in the diff.
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Git's similarity index and color-moved marks name a path change and a relocated block. The diff UI shows that relationship. A pure move or copy is the paths and the score, with no delete block and no add block. A copy no longer steals the source file's blob.

Co-authored-by: Máté Molnár <matemolnar8@users.noreply.github.com>
